content.title: Tennessee basketball defeats Virginia, advances to Sweet 16
content.text: Updated March 22, 2026, 9:32 p.m. ETNo. 6 seed Tennessee (24-11) defeated No. 3 seed Virginia (30-6), 79-72, Sunday in a NCAA Tournament second-round game.Tennessee is the first team to defeat two 30-team wins in the opening rounds since the field expanded to 64 teams in 1985.The Vols led, 36-31, a halftime.Ja'Kopbi Gillespie totaled 21 points, six assists, three rebounds and one steal. He converted 6-of-14 field goal attempts, 3-of-5 three-point attempts and 6-of-6 free throw attempts. Gillespie was one of five Tennessee players to score 10-plus points in the contest against the Cavaliers.Nate Ament recorded 16 points, four rebounds, one steal and one block, while Bishop Boswell had 13 points and a career-high nine assists.J.P. Estrella and Jaylen Carey scored 10 points each for the Vols. Estrella also had five rebounds, one assist and one steal, while Carey finished with two rebounds and one assist.Virginia's Thijs De Ridder led all scorers with 22 points.Vols Wire provided live game updates between Tennessee and Virginia and are listed below.Tennessee versus Virginia basketball live game updates Final: Tennessee 79, Virginia 72Vols advance to the Sweet 16 with win over Cavaliers.Tennessee 70, Virginia 68Vols lead with 2:39 remaining in the game.Tennessee 66, Virginia 64Vols call timeout, leading by two with 5:23 remaining.Tennessee 63, Virginia 58Vols lead the Cavaliers with 7:28 remaining in the game.Tennessee 57, Virginia 51The Vols lead rhe Cavaliers with 10:11 remaining in the game.
